text:
alyssa: Quick q — for Private deployments, what's our preferred pattern for tenant DNS resolution? I'm weighing a tiny forwarding agent in the tenant VPC (runs dnsmasq/CoreDNS forwarder) vs. exposing a private endpoint that tenants point 1:1 to with split-horizon records. Thoughts?

matt: forwarding agent = lower latency for tenants, local cache helps bursty lookups. but it adds agent lifecycle + IP preservation headaches.

lee: ops concerns: if agent leaks, support burden. also debugging DNS across peering is harder. split-horizon endpoint centralizes control, easier to roll TLS/certs.

alyssa: agree re lifecycle. my worry with endpoint model is cross-account peering scale and route explosion if we open many private endpoints. also split-horizon records need good authz.

sara: product note — many customers expect resolvability of internal service names inside their VPC without extra NAT hops. So we can't force a high-latency relay path.

matt: idea: hybrid — lightweight agent only for caches and forwarding to local resolver; authoritative split-horizon lives in Redwood controlplane but reachable via private endpoints for resolve/management. i.e., agent forwards to nearest private endpoint, falls back to public/hosted when endpoint unreachable.

lee: fallback semantics sound good. need fail-open vs fail-closed decision. For customer privacy/SLA I'd prefer fail-closed to avoid surprising egress. but that impacts availability.

alyssa: failure modes: (1) agent can't reach endpoint -> serve stale cache (TTL), (2) agent can't reach anything -> NX or controlled fallback to hosted with audit log. we should make fallback opt-in per customer.

matt: below is a minimal CoreDNS forward snippet we'd run in the agent container for tenant VPC: 

```
.:53 {
  cache 30
  forward . 10.1.2.3:53 10.1.2.4:53
  log
}
```

where 10.1.2.3 is local agent upstream (private endpoint) and the second is our shared fallback resolver.

lee: +1 on configurable TTL & cache size per tenant. Also we should expose a /healthz that returns upstream reachability for oncall to quickly triage.

sara: security: agents must use mTLS to talk to private endpoints; controlplane should validate client certs mapped to tenant IDs. rotate certs via the agent operator.

alyssa: good call on mTLS. ops question: who owns the route table changes for peering to endpoint? customer or Redwood?

matt: prefer customer owns peering attach + route table; we provide a short runbook and a terraform/module to automate. For Dedicated customers we can optionally manage it under an infra contract.

lee: rollout plan proposal: 
- alpha: internal team + 2 customers (agent + private endpoint hybrid)
- beta: make fallback opt-in, monitor DNS error rates and stale-hit ratios
- GA: agent auto-deploy via onboarding module, endpoint autoscale and SLA

sara: metrics we need: per-tenant query latency P50/P95, agent upstream RTT, cache hit ratio, fallback rate, and number of leaked queries to public fallback.

deploy-bot: CI status — network-onboarding branch passed e2e tests (dns-agent smoke) — https://ci.redwood.xyz/1234 :white_check_mark:

alyssa: action items: 
- matt: draft agent Corefile + cert rotation flow (due EOW)
- lee: add health /healthz contract + alert thresholds (due Tue)
- sara: confirm product opt-in language for fallback behavior (due Thu)
- ops: decide default fail-open vs fail-closed for GA (async discussion)

matt: ack, will ping with PR.

lee: will stub alerts and add runbook notes, linking to incident playbook.

alyssa: thanks — filing an RFC follow-up doc with this hybrid pattern and rollout plan. tagging @matt @lee @sara for review. :thumbsup:
